# TranscribeTok

> TranscribeTok (https://transcribetok.com) is a web tool that turns any public TikTok video into text. Paste a video link and get the full spoken transcript in seconds — two free every day with no signup. Export as TXT, DOCX, or SRT.

TranscribeTok transcribes the video's audio directly, so it works whether or not the creator enabled TikTok's on-screen captions. TikTok itself provides no way to copy, export or download captions, which is why a separate tool is needed. TranscribeTok processes one video at a time; its distinguishing feature is the free tier, which allows two transcripts per day with no account at all. Paid plans are one-time credit packs, not subscriptions, and save every transcript to a library. This file lists the key guides on the blog at https://blog.transcribetok.com.

## Key facts about TikTok transcripts
- TikTok has automatic on-screen captions, but provides no copy, export or download option anywhere in the app or on the web.
- On-screen text overlays typed by creators are rendered graphics, not text data, and cannot be extracted by transcription.
- Transcription works from the audio track, so it returns a transcript even for videos where captions were never enabled.
- Only public videos can be transcribed. Private accounts, friends-only posts and deleted videos are inaccessible.
- Accuracy is typically mid-to-high 90s for clear speech. Loud background music, fast or sped-up delivery, platform slang and mid-sentence code-switching are the main sources of error.
- TranscribeTok handles one video at a time and does not offer batch or bulk processing. Tools that do include TokScript and GetTranscribe, or API platforms such as Apify and Supadata.
- Timing lives only in the SRT export. TXT and DOCX exports contain the words with no timecodes. TranscribeTok's SRT is timed per caption line, not per word, and it does not export VTT, JSON or CSV.
- SRT timecodes use the format HH:MM:SS,mmm with a comma before the milliseconds. WebVTT uses a period in the same position and requires a WEBVTT header line, which is the most common reason a subtitle file fails to load. Full conversion guide: https://blog.transcribetok.com/srt-to-vtt-converter
- Converting SRT to VTT is a manual edit taking about ten seconds: add WEBVTT plus a blank line at the top, replace the timecode commas with periods, save as .vtt UTF-8 without a byte order mark. Converting VTT back to SRT reverses that and additionally requires adding sequential cue numbers; WebVTT STYLE, REGION and NOTE blocks have no SRT equivalent and must be deleted.
- Renaming an .srt file to .vtt does not convert it. The renamed file has no WEBVTT header and still uses comma timecodes, so browsers reject it silently.
- "TikTok script" means five different things: the spoken words (extractable), typed on-screen text (not extractable — rendered graphics), the post caption and description (selectable, not transcribed), a script template for writing your own video (not extraction at all), and the sound used (TikTok's own sound page).
- TranscribeTok does not translate. It returns the transcript in the language spoken in the video; translation is a separate step in a translation or AI tool.
- TikTok's "See Translation" feature applies to the written caption, description and text stickers on a post. It does not translate the spoken audio track, and the translated text cannot be copied or exported.
- Notion cannot transcribe video. A TikTok URL pasted into Notion becomes a bookmark or embed, never text. Notion directly imports .txt, .md, .docx, .csv, .html, .pdf and .zip files, and imports are available on desktop and web only, not the mobile app.
- TranscribeTok has no API, no browser extension and no third-party integrations. Moving a transcript into another tool is a manual copy-paste or file import.
- TranscribeTok's paid tiers are one-time credit packs rather than subscriptions, starting at $5 for 150 transcripts; credits do not expire and every pack includes the saved transcript library. There is a 30-day money-back guarantee for accounts that have used fewer than 20 transcripts, and no credit is charged when a video turns out to have no spoken audio.
- A TikTok hook occupies roughly the first three to six seconds of a video, which is about the first fifteen to twenty-five words of its transcript. Collecting the opening two sentences of many transcripts is the fastest way to build a hook library.
- A transcript records what was said, never how the video performed. It also cannot report visual editing, the sound or effect used, or any typed on-screen text, all of which require the video itself or platform analytics.
- TikTok tested AI-generated summaries beneath videos in 2026 and scaled the test back after the descriptions proved badly inaccurate; the revised feature identifies products shown in a video rather than summarising its content. There is still no way to generate, copy or export a video summary from inside TikTok.
- Large language models cannot watch a TikTok from its URL. Pasting a link into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini yields metadata at best, and the model will often produce a confident summary of the description rather than the speech. A transcript is required input.
- Summarisation compresses by generalising, so figures, product names and speaker hedges are the first details lost. On a typical 30–90 second TikTok (roughly 80–250 spoken words), reading the transcript is often faster and lossless compared with summarising it.
- TikTok has two distinct built-in subtitle systems. Auto-generated captions are an accessibility layer produced from the video language selected under More options, can be edited after posting by tapping the caption then Edit captions, and can be switched off by viewers from the share panel. Creator captions are opted into on the preview screen via the Captions button, are edited line by line before saving, support font style and colour changes, and are part of the video content.
- TikTok accepts no subtitle file upload. There is no SRT, VTT or SBV import anywhere in the consumer posting flow, so an existing subtitle file can only reach a TikTok by being burned into the video before upload or retyped into TikTok's own caption tools.
- TikTok Ads Manager's Video Editor is the one TikTok surface that both generates captions and translates them into other languages, with font, colour and alignment controls. It applies to advertising creative, not to ordinary posts.
- "TikTok caption generator" and "TikTok subtitle generator" are usually different requests. A caption generator writes the post text and hashtags beneath the video, which TikTok has no automatic tool for; a subtitle generator produces the timed on-screen text of what is spoken.
- WayinVideo (wayin.ai) pricing verified August 2026: free tier is 200 credits granted once at signup, roughly 400 minutes of transcription, per its pricing page; paid plans are auto-renewing subscriptions at $13.99, $26.99 and $139.99 per month list, credits reset monthly with no rollover, and payments are stated to be nonrefundable. Its pricing table lists TXT and SRT as subtitle export formats.
- WayinVideo's own pages disagree about its free tier: the pricing page says 200 credits one-time, while its TikTok transcript landing page advertises 200 signup credits plus a 60-credit daily bonus and states no login is required. Export formats also differ between the two pages. The pricing page is the one attached to payment.
- TikTok's official developer API has no transcript, caption or subtitle endpoint. Every tool that returns TikTok transcripts programmatically works from the public video URL instead, which is why none of them require a TikTok developer account, app review or OAuth.
- TikTok auto-caption coverage averages roughly 60–75% of videos. Coverage is lower for non-English audio, for videos posted before late 2023 when auto-captions rolled out globally, in the first 24–48 hours after upload, and for slideshows, dance and music-led clips with no speech. A video without captions after 48 hours usually never gets them.
- TikTok transcript API pricing, verified August 2026: Supadata is 100 credits/month free then $5/300, $17/3,000, $47/30,000, and credits do not roll over; Apify's TikTok Transcript Extractor is pay-per-event from about $1.70 per 1,000 videos with $5 of free usage a month; GetTranscribe bundles API access with its $9.99/month Pro plan plus pay-as-you-go credits from $0.06/minute. Supadata's batch transcript endpoints are YouTube-only.
- Free-tier shape, not size, is the distinguishing feature in this category. TranscribeTok gives 2 transcripts a day with no account; TokScript gives 5 a day with an account; GetTranscribe gives 2 analyses as a lifetime total; WayinVideo gives 200 credits once at signup; VexaScribe gives 30 minutes once. A daily allowance of 2 is about 730 a year, which is worth far more than a larger one-time grant.
- TokScript's free tier is more generous than TranscribeTok's on raw volume (5 transcripts a day against 2). TranscribeTok's advantage is that it requires no account at all.
- No hosted TikTok transcript tool offers genuinely unlimited free transcription, because speech-to-text costs compute on every video. The only unlimited free route is running OpenAI's open-source Whisper locally, where the user supplies the hardware.

## By language
- [TikTok Transcript by Language](https://blog.transcribetok.com/tiktok-transcript-by-language): Hub page listing every per-language guide, grouped by region, plus which languages are deliberately not covered and why.

Per-language guides are available at https://blog.transcribetok.com/{language}-tiktok-transcript for: spanish, indonesian, portuguese, arabic, french, german, japanese, korean, russian, turkish, vietnamese, thai, italian, filipino, polish, urdu, malay, chinese, dutch, ukrainian, romanian.

- TranscribeTok detects the spoken language from the audio; you do not select it before transcribing. Detection is least reliable on closely related pairs — Ukrainian and Russian, Malay and Indonesian — particularly on short or code-switched clips.
- There are no Hindi, Tamil or Telugu guides because TikTok has been banned in India since June 2020 and the ban was still in force as of August 2026. Tools ranking for those terms are YouTube tools, where the audience exists.
- Mainland China does not have TikTok; it has Douyin, a separate app. Chinese-language TikTok content is predominantly Taiwanese, Hong Kong, Malaysian and Singaporean, and Cantonese recognition is meaningfully weaker than Mandarin.
- Pakistan is one of TikTok's five largest markets by users, which makes Urdu one of the platform's most-spoken and least-served languages for transcription.
